name: Radcore NeutronShield RZ-9 Reactor Entry Suit
description:
A full-envelope radiation suit in matte lead-gray with fluorescent amber warning strips running diagonally across the torso and down both legs. The outer layer is woven neutron-scatter fabric — boron-filament threaded through a dense polyimide base — with a rigid chest plate housing an embedded dosimeter display visible through a small scratch-resistant window. Bulky but articulated at the hip and shoulder with accordion-fold gussets.

Designed for reactor maintenance crews working hot zones in GLMZ's aging fission grid and the contaminated industrial sectors of the Gray Zone. The suit's amber strips fade to cream with cumulative radiation exposure — a passive wear indicator most supervisors pretend not to notice.
functionality: Rated for 12-hour low-to-moderate radiation exposure in reactor maintenance zones. Integrated chest dosimeter logs cumulative dose and triggers a haptic pulse at threshold. Accordion gussets allow full crouch and crawl movement. Compatible with standard CBRN respirator collar mounts.
what_it_says: You go into the places that slowly kill you, and the suit keeps score.
worn_by: the Gray Zone scavengers who got lucky enough to find one
story_hooks: A suit returned from a the Gray Zone remediation job has a dosimeter log showing exposure levels that should have been fatal — the worker who wore it is fine, and no one can explain why.
Radcore's RZ-9 is the standard-issue suit for a reactor zone that officially doesn't exist on any GLMZ infrastructure map.
The amber warning strips on a supervisor's suit haven't faded in three years of reactor work — someone has been replacing them before inspections.

physical_description.visual_profile: A bulky, utilitarian full-body suit with an industrial silhouette dominated by protective volume. Matte lead-gray base punctuated by diagonal fluorescent amber warning stripes creating a chevron pattern across the torso and legs. The chest features a prominent rectangular dosimeter window that catches light. Overall impression: hazmat worker, reactor engineer, occupational survival gear.
physical_description.fit: Deliberately oversized and box-cut to accommodate layering and movement in contaminated environments. Articulated gussets at hips, shoulders, and elbows allow articulation despite bulk. Compression at wrists and ankles with friction-sealed cuffs. Intentionally not form-fitting—safety over aesthetics.
physical_description.primary_material: Boron-filament neutron-scatter weave (polyimide base), lead-infused outer layer, scratch-resistant polymer window panel over dosimeter housing
physical_description.texture: Dense, rigid weave with a matte finish that diffuses light. The accordion-fold gussets create visible ribbed panels. Faintly grainy surface texture from boron thread integration. High-friction fabric designed to resist snags.
physical_description.color_scheme: Matte lead-gray primary with fluorescent amber diagonal stripes (60° angle, spaced 12cm apart). Stripes fade progressively to cream/pale yellow in worn areas—passive cumulative exposure indicator.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snap across the chest over a friction-sealed primary seam. Sealed cuff locks at wrists and ankles using bayonet-twist connectors. No traditional zippers—magnetic panel system throughout.
distinctive_features: Embedded dosimeter display window (5cm × 3cm, recessed in rigid chest plate)
Diagonal fluorescent warning stripe pattern with radiation-fading property
Accordion-fold accordion gussets at major joints for mobility despite bulk
Boron-filament weave visible as slight surface texture
Radcore branding on left shoulder (industrial sans-serif)
Inspection tag pocket on right thigh (faded/worn)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 industrial working class. High-spec safety equipment supplied by employers rather than personal purchase. Maintenance crews, reactor techs, hot-zone specialists.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by those in the most hazardous sectors of GLMZ infrastructure—the aging GLMZ fission grid, the Gray Zone's contaminated zones, decommissioned reactor maintenance. Signals industrial reliability, acceptance of biological risk, and stoic occupational fatalism. The fading amber stripes are an unspoken record of cumulative exposure that most wearers avoid discussing.
physical_description.condition_typical: Heavily patched at stress points (shoulders, elbows, crotch gusset). Faded amber stripes indicating months of active use. Scuff marks and minor tears sealed with gray repair tape. The dosimeter window often clouded or cracked. Hem weighted with additional lead patches from field repairs.
